source.title: A shared inhibitory circuit for both exogenous and endogenous control of stimulus selection

confidence_rationale: The strongest available evidence that biology implements a DEDICATED, anatomically separable pre-selection suppression substrate rather than folding suppression into the priority map -- causal inactivation, single-unit recording, and both exogenous and endogenous routes through one circuit. Discounted for the avian midbrain preparation and for the gap between a spatial space-map and REE's non-spatial cue routing.
failure_signatures: Inactivating Imc ABOLISHED competitive selection entirely -- selection did not degrade gracefully to a facilitation-only mode, so a priority map without a dedicated inhibitory partner may not select at all under competition rather than selecting worse.

The same circuit carried BOTH exogenous and endogenous suppression; an architecture that implements bottom-up salience competition and top-down goal biasing through separate mechanisms diverges from this organisation.
Suppression was global across the entire tectal space map from a spatially precise input -- a local or pairwise inhibition scheme does not reproduce this.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Focal reversible inactivation of the nucleus isthmi pars magnocellularis, a single inhibitory circuit in the barn owl midbrain tegmentum, abolished both stimulus-driven and internally driven competitive interactions in the optic tectum; Imc neurons transform spatially precise multisensory and endogenous input into inhibitory output suppressing competing representations across the entire tectal space map.
mapping.ree_translation: REE reads this as the affirmative case for Q-082: biology does implement an explicit, anatomically distinct pre-selection suppression substrate, positioned before the competing representations acquire behavioural control, and shared between bottom-up and top-down routes. If REE's mechanisms are predominantly post-entry -- write gating, persistence, conflict handling, mode hysteresis -- this is the specific thing REE lacks.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Barn owl midbrain, a retinotopic SPATIAL space map with an explicit spatial competition problem. REE's precision-weighted cue routing is not spatial and its MECH-254 top-k boundary bottleneck is a capacity limit rather than a space map, so 'suppression across the space map' has no direct structural counterpart. The inference that REE needs an analogous substrate presumes the top-k bottleneck fails to do this work -- which is exactly the MECH-467 leg 3 gate Q-082 is registered behind, and is NOT settled by this paper.
mapping.source_context: Barn owl (Tyto alba), midbrain optic tectum and nucleus isthmi, single-unit recording with focal reversible pharmacological inactivation, multisensory and endogenous stimulus competition.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high -- causal inactivation with single-unit readout in Nature Neuroscience is close to the ceiling for this kind of claim. Transfer risk is the binding constraint: avian midbrain spatial space map to a non-spatial artificial cue-routing architecture is a long transfer, and the homologous mammalian circuit (parabigeminal nucleus) is less well characterised functionally.
